reasoning: iter-052: switch project_full_fused per_gaussian dispatch from strided to block-chunked (same rationale as iter-051 for the gauss_rec prelude). project writes contiguous per-Gaussian records to means_2d (8 B), covs_2d (16 B), depths (4 B), and radii_scratch (8 B). With strided dispatch (i=w; i+=W) and W=10, adjacent records were owned by different workers — most output cache lines (64 B) covered Gaussians [w, w+1, ..., w+15] across all 10 workers, causing systematic cross-core line invalidation as each worker stored into 'its' Gaussian. Block-chunked dispatch gives each worker a contiguous private span, eliminating cross-core line traffic and letting the hw prefetcher engage on the sequential reads of cov3d/means/extrinsics inputs. Result: sum_total 306.6 -> 288.2 ms (-6%, -18 ms / 30 frames). project stage saw the biggest share of the savings (~17 ms). PSNR identical. Same pattern likely wins on the remaining strided loops in tile_assign and the per-stage gathers — next iters will roll it out.
